REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - JANUARY 26, 2023 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
* COVID-19 NOTICE *
To protect public health and safety during the COVID-19 pandemic and in compliance with the current State Department of Public Health and Los Angeles County Health Officer Orders and City of Cerritos COVID-19 Safety Plan, the City Council Chamber will be open to the public. As authorized by State of California Executive Orders N-25-20, N-29-20, and N-08-21, and subsequently by Assembly Bill 361 (Chapter 165, Statutes of 2021) and City Council Resolution No. 2022-10 adopted pursuant thereto, this meeting may also be conducted via teleconference, if necessary. Public observation and participation in this meeting will be facilitated through the methods described below.
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in-person in the Council Chamber subject to posted COVID-19 protocols.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in-person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY,
JANUARY 26, 2023, 7:00 P.M., IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL,
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Juno Smalley, New Life Community Church.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Cerritos Aquatic Club.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Lynda P. Johnson
  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Bruce Barrows
  Mayor/Chair Chuong Vo

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  A proclamation was made by the City Council as follows:

  Mariposa Escrow (Business Spotlight).

5B.  Review and consideration of appointments, removals, and filling of scheduled or unscheduled
  vacancies on the Cerritos Advisory Boards (2022-24 term) (COUNCIL).

  There was no action taken on this item.

5C.  Informational update on the City’s response to the COVID-19 pandemic and other City
  events, services, and programs.

  An informational update was given by Annie Hylton, City Librarian & Marketing Manager. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  There was no action taken on this item.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Tamara Hill, representing Philip Liberatore, CPA, thanked members of the City Council
  who attended their business open house on January 21, 2023.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the
  Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  DEVELOPMENT CODE AMENDMENT 2022-1, A REQUEST TO AMEND VARIOUS
  PROVISIONS OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE ALLOWING FOR DRIVE-THROUGH
  SERVICE RESTAURANTS TO BE CONDITIONALLY PERMITTED IN THE COMMUNITY
  COMMERCIAL (CC) AND NEIGHBORHOOD COMMERCIAL (CN) ZONES, AND
  AMENDING REGULATIONS FOR THE LOCATION OF THESE USES IN THE CITY OF

8A.  (continued)

  CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT 2022-1, A REQUEST BY THE TARGET CORPORATION TO
  PERMIT A DRIVE-THROUGH SERVICE RESTAURANT AT 20200 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE,
  CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA, 90703. THE SUBJECT PROPERTY IS ZONED

  PRECISE PLAN 2022-1, A PROPOSAL BY THE TARGET CORPORATION TO DEMOLISH A
  VACANT TARGET GARDEN CENTER, TO CONSTRUCT A NEW DRIVE-THROUGH
  SERVICE RESTAURANT, AND TO COMPLETE OTHER RELATED SITE IMPROVEMENTS
  AT 20200 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA, 90703. THE SUBJECT
  PROPERTY IS ZONED NEIGHBORHOOD COMMERCIAL (CN) (APN 7044-016-006)
  (COUNCIL).*

  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) for Development Code Amendment 2022-1,
  Tentative Parcel Map 83312, Conditional Use Permit 2022-1, and Precise Plan 2022-

  Staff reports were given by Sabrina Chan, Advance Planning Manager and Sandy
  Cisneros, Current Planning Manager. A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  Councilmember Johnson disclosed that she viewed the December 7, 2022 and January
  11, 2023 Planning Commission meetings as related to this project and was familiar with
  the comments which were stated at each meeting. Councilmember Johnson further
  disclosed that on January 25, 2023 she met with representatives of the project
  applicants, EKA Consulting Engineers and Property Nine Development, at Cerritos City
  Hall per the applicant’s request. City Manager Art Gallucci and other members of staff
  were also in attendance at the January 25, 2023 meeting.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments period.

  In-Person Public Comments:

  David Pylman requested traffic statistics for Lakewood and Cerritos as related to the
  subject project and further requested the City Council separately consider Citywide
  drive-through uses prior to further consideration of this specific project.

  Michael DiGangi, representing the applicant, Property Nine Development, responded to
  various inquiries from the City Council and public speakers.

  Al Barlevy expressed support for City Council approval of the subject project.

  Sandra Hojo expressed concerns regarding the traffic impacts of the project on the
  adjacent neighborhoods. She requested the City Council separately consider Citywide
  drive-through uses prior to further consideration of this specific project.

  Written Correspondence:
  (Written correspondence is considered public record. Full-text copies of submitted
  written correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  Marty and Gail Grossman expressed opposition to the subject project, citing negative
  community impacts.

City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 4 of 9

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the
  Mayor closed public comments and declared the public hearing closed.

  MAIN MOTION: A motion was made by Solanki, and seconded by Barrows, to include
  an additional condition of approval for the subject project to require both driveways on
  the Del Amo Boulevard side adjacent to the property to be “right turn only” and require
  the applicant to fund the installation of a center median, subject to staff’s approval of
  the design, on Del Amo Boulevard adjacent to the subject property (COUNCIL).

  SUBSTITUTE MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Johnson, as modified
  to:

  1. Reverse the recommendation of the Planning Commission and approve the proposed
  project, inclusive of Development Code Amendment 2022-1, Tentative Parcel Map
  83312, Conditional Use Permit 2022-1, and Precise Plan 2022-1, and approving and
  certifying the Mitigated Negative Declaration for the proposed project;

  2. Approve the following additional condition of approval:

  Residual Traffic Assessment. A six (6) month review period shall be
  established from the date that Starbuck’s Coffee is granted occupancy to
  appropriately assess residual traffic impacts as a result of the drive-through
  service restaurant. The review/assessment shall be in the form of a traffic impact
  analysis, paid for by the developer as a developer deposit prior to being granted
  occupancy. The initial deposit shall be used to cover actual costs for the traffic
  impact analysis, such that any balance remaining will be returned to the
  applicant, or if additional funds are needed to complete the analysis, the
  applicant shall provide an additional deposit as required to cover the actual costs
  of the analysis. If, as a result of the traffic impact assessment, any reasonable
  traffic related improvements are necessary (including the imposition of a “no left
  turn” requirement and corresponding signage from the two parking access
  driveways and/or installation of a raised median on Bloomfield Avenue and/or
  Del Amo Blvd.) to improve vehicular/pedestrian safety or to alleviate parking lot
  and/or arterial street traffic congestion caused by “stacking” of vehicles at the
  drive-through of the restaurant, as determined by the City Engineer, then said
  improvements shall be completed by the developer with all costs related to such
  improvements paid for by the developer;

  3. Waive full reading of and adopt Resolution No. 2023-06, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY OF CERRITOS APPROVING AND CERTIFYING A MITIGATED NEGATIVE
  DECLARATION FOR A PROPOSED DRIVE-THROUGH SERVICE RESTAURANT
  UNDER PRECISE PLAN 2022-1 AND RELATED ENTITLEMENTS (APN 7044-
  016-006) (COUNCIL);

  TARGET CORPORATION TO DEMOLISH A VACANT TARGET GARDEN CENTER,

  AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA, 90703. THE SUBJECT PROPERTY IS
  ZONED NEIGHBORHOOD COMMERCIAL (CN) (APN 7044-016-006) (COUNCIL).

  AYES:  Johnson, Solanki, Yokoyama, Barrows, Vo
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
